memberdef.name: AlignedAndConstrainedPointing

briefdescription.para: Construct a flight profile with constrained pointing.

detaileddescription.para:
This solves the "align and constrain" (two-vector) attitude problem at each instant of the orbit. Fully defining the spacecraft attitude requires fixing 3 rotational degrees of freedom, which is done using two constraints of decreasing priority:
Alignment (primary constraint): the body frame direction of the alignment pointing constraint is pointed exactly towards its target (e.g. the payload boresight towards geodetic nadir). This fixes 2 degrees of freedom, leaving the spacecraft free to rotate about its alignment direction.
Clocking (secondary constraint): the remaining degree of freedom (the rotation about the alignment direction) is fixed by rotating the body frame direction of the clocking pointing constraint as close as possible to its target (e.g. a body axis along the ground velocity, for yaw steering).

The celestial object of the orbit is used for the target types that depend on the rotation or shape of the central body (geodetic nadir, ECEF velocity and sliding ground velocity). See AlignAndConstrainGenerator for details on how the orientation is computed.

parameterdescription.para: An alignment pointing constraint (primary constraint, met exactly)
A clocking pointing constraint (secondary constraint, met as closely as possible)
An angular offset applied to the clocking target, as a right-handed rotation about the alignment target

memberdef.name: AlignAndConstrainGenerator

briefdescription.para: Generate a function that returns a quaternion constrained by alignment and clocking vectors for each given state.

detaileddescription.para: The generated function solves the "align and constrain" (two-vector) attitude problem: the spacecraft alignment body frame direction is pointed exactly towards the alignment target (primary constraint), and the spacecraft is then rotated about this direction so that its clocking body frame direction gets as close as possible to the clocking target (secondary constraint).

For each state, with all target directions expressed in GCRF:
The alignment target direction is computed from the alignment pointing constraint.
The clocking target direction is computed from the clocking pointing constraint, then projected onto the plane perpendicular to the alignment target direction, and rotated about the alignment target direction by the angular clocking offset.
The clocking body frame direction is projected onto the plane perpendicular to the alignment body frame direction.
The returned quaternion is the rotation from GCRF to the spacecraft body frame that maps the alignment target direction onto the alignment body frame direction, and the projected clocking target direction onto the projected clocking body frame direction.
The resulting attitude is undefined if the alignment and clocking target directions are colinear at a given state, as there is no unique rotation about the alignment target direction in that case.
This function is typically used in conjunction with CustomPointing, or directly through AlignedAndConstrainedPointing.

parameterdescription.para: If the alignment and clocking pointing constraints have the same target type (except for trajectory position and trajectory velocity targets, which can point to different trajectories)
If the alignment and clocking body frame directions are colinear
If the alignment and clocking targets are geocentric nadir and geodetic nadir
